summary: Order placement latency/timeouts originate from portfolio-service deploy dep-5905 (v4.5.0, rolled out 08:56:32Z) which added an unindexed query on the shared ledger-db's 48M-row trades table (Seq Scan on trades, rows=48211907). The full-table scans drove ledger-db CPU from ~30% to ~96% and saturated its connections, starving order-service's INSERT INTO orders and causing statement timeouts. Both affected services (portfolio-service, order-service) are the two that query trades/orders heavily; the anomaly begins exactly in the first metric bucket after the deploy (08:58), while the earlier 08:00 autovacuum config change left CPU flat at ~30% for 56 minutes and is not the trigger. Root cause is a bad_deployment in portfolio-service; order-service is a downstream victim of the shared database saturation.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deployment: portfolio-service v4.5.0 unindexed trades query saturates shared ledger-db, starving order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: portfolio-service deploy dep-5905 (v4.5.0, 08:56) introduced a query on the 48M-row trades table filtered by account_id + executed_at with no supporting index ('no migration included'). Postgres runs a Seq Scan on trades (~48M rows) per request, driving ledger-db CPU to ~96% and consuming connections. The shared ledger-db becomes CPU/connection starved, so order-service's INSERT INTO orders exceed their statement timeout, producing order-placement slowness and timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 deploys new trades query with no index at 08:56
First bad buckets and first portfolio slow query appear at 08:58 (portfolio p99 185->6963ms, ledger-db CPU 30->96%, order p99 151->2878ms)
ledger-db logs Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907) application_name=portfolio-service, ~140 slow queries/min
Shared ledger-db saturates; portfolio and order db pools peg (12->50, 14->46)
order-service INSERT INTO orders hit statement timeout against ledger-db

assumptions: The deploy's new query is the direct source of the trades Seq Scan (query text matches change summary).
order-service's INSERT INTO orders is contending on the same CPU-bound ledger-db instance.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change: aggressive autovacuum on ledger-db (cfg-2903) causes CPU/IO saturation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The DBA's 08:00 autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor change (0.2->0.1) made autovacuum far more aggressive on the 48M-row trades table, saturating ledger-db CPU and slowing all queries, including order-service inserts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing does not fit: the config change is at 08:00 but ledger-db CPU stayed flat at ~30% for 56 minutes and only spiked at 08:58, exactly when dep-5905 rolled out. The slow queries are explicitly attributed to application_name=portfolio-service with a Seq Scan on trades, not autovacuum.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / infrastructure failure at ledger-db (CPU, IOPS or connections)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db itself ran out of a resource (CPU/IOPS/connections) independent of any release, degrading all dependent services.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The CPU spike is a consequence of the deployed seq-scan workload (query text and application_name=portfolio-service prove the source) and starts only after the 08:56 deploy. Disk and replication lag were normal (F12). No faulty node/broker.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External dependency (exchange-api / market-data) failure propagating to order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A degradation of an external provider or market-data dependency slowed order placement.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: All order-service errors are ledger-db statement timeouts (INSERT INTO orders), not exchange/gateway errors; the onset coincides with ledger-db CPU saturation and the portfolio deploy.

facts.statement: order-service p99 rose from ~151ms (08:56) to 2878ms avg / 5607ms max (08:58) and stayed ~5.2s.
portfolio-service p99 rose from ~185ms (08:56) to 6963ms (08:58) and stayed ~7s.
ledger-db CPU rose from ~30% (08:56) to ~96% (08:58) and stayed saturated.
ledger-db slow queries went from ~1/min to ~140/min.
The dominant slow query is a Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907) attributed to application_name=portfolio-service, first at 08:58:38.
portfolio-service dep-5905 v4.5.0 rolled out at 08:56:32 adding an unindexed trades query with 'no migration included'.
The only config change was ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1 at 08:00.
order-service errors are all ledger-db INSERT INTO orders statement timeouts; error_rate ~9.4%, pool 14->46.
portfolio-service db pool pegged at 50; its error_rate stayed flat (~0.2%).
ledger-db is shared by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service.
payment-service and settlement-service latencies stayed flat.
ledger-db disk usage (~71%) and replication lag (~40ms) were normal.
HIST-111 precedent: unindexed report query caused trades seq scans / high db cpu.

assumptions: The deploy's new 'query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' is the literal source of the logged Seq Scan query (text matches).
order-service INSERT INTO orders and portfolio SELECT share the same ledger-db instance and contend for its CPU/connections.
The 2-minute metric buckets are aligned such that the 08:56 bucket predates the deploy's effect, making 08:58 the first affected bucket.

timeline.event: DBA config change cfg-2903 on ledger-db: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 (more aggressive autovacuum). No metric change follows.
portfolio-service deploy dep-5905 (v4.5.0) adds a new unindexed query on trades; no migration included.
dep-5905 rollout complete, all pods ready.
First bad metric bucket: portfolio p99 185->6963ms, order p99 151->2878ms, ledger-db CPU 30->96%, slow queries spike.
First ledger-db slow query: Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907) application_name=portfolio-service.
First order-service error: ledger-db statement timeout on INSERT INTO orders.
Incident INC-009 reported (SEV-1); condition persists through 10:59 with no recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back portfolio-service to the previous version (pre-v4.5.0) to stop the seq-scan workload on ledger-db and confirm ledger-db CPU and order-service latency recover.
recommended_actions.rationale: Removal of the offending query is the fastest way to restore the shared database; the fault was introduced by dep-5905.

recommended_actions.action: Add a composite index on trades(account_id, executed_at) (or equivalent) and deploy it via a proper migration, then re-introduce the query.
recommended_actions.rationale: The Seq Scan on 48M rows is the direct cause; the change summary noted 'no migration included'. Mirrors HIST-111 resolution.

recommended_actions.action: Add a CI/query-review gate that blocks unindexed full-table scans on large shared tables before deployment.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence; HIST-111's resolution explicitly called for a query review gate.

recommended_actions.action: Isolate heavy analytical/reporting queries from the transactional order path (separate replica or resource-group for portfolio/reporting).
recommended_actions.rationale: Order placement shares a single CPU-bound ledger-db with portfolio reporting; isolation prevents a reporting regression from taking down order placement.

data_gaps: No EXPLAIN plan or schema/index listing for the trades table was available; the absence of the index is inferred from the logged 'Seq Scan on trades' and the deploy's 'no migration included'.

Ledger-db logs only expose WARN-level slow-query entries after 08:58; no autovacuum activity logs were returned, so the 08:00 config change's immediate behavior could not be directly observed (only that CPU stayed flat until 08:56).

No per-query connection/waits attribution on ledger-db to prove exactly which callers were starved vs. served; order-service starvation is inferred from its own timeout errors plus overall connection saturation.

findings.statement: order-service p99 latency was normal (~148-165ms) until the 08:56 bucket, then jumped at 08:58 to 2878ms avg / max 5607ms and stayed ~5.2s through 10:50.
portfolio-service p99 latency was flat (~175-185ms) through 08:56, then jumped at 08:58 to 6963ms and stayed ~7s.
ledger-db CPU was ~30% through 08:56, then jumped to ~96% at 08:58 and stayed saturated.
ledger-db slow queries were ~1/min until 08:30, then spiked in the 08:45-09:00 bucket (avg 19.48, max 139.68) and reached ~140/min from 09:00.
The dominant slow query at ledger-db is a Seq Scan on the trades table (rows=48211907) attributed to application_name=portfolio-service, first seen 08:58:38.

order-service errors are exclusively 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' against ledger-db, first seen 09:00:42; error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~9.4%, and db_pool_in_use rose from ~14 to ~46.

findings.statement: portfolio-service's db_pool_in_use jumped from ~12 to pegged at its max of 50 at 08:45-09:00 onward, while its error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% (it is slow but not erroring).
ledger-db is a shared datastore used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
payment-service and settlement-service latencies were flat across the whole incident window (payment ~317-324ms, settlement ~236-247ms), despite also depending on ledger-db.
No disk pressure on ledger-db (disk_used_pct ~71% flat) and no replication lag (replication_lag_ms ~40ms flat) during the incident.

Historical incident HIST-111 is an exact precedent: a new report query without an index caused sequential scans that slowed ledger-db, root cause bad_deployment, resolution 'Added index; query review gate'.
